To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is impossible for massive spin-2 gauge bosons to unitarize 2->2 scatterings at tree level.

(a) tree-level unitarization is possible in a theory that includes massive spin-1, spin-2, and spin-0 particles, (b) tree-level unitarity is unachievable in a theory that only contains massive spin-2 particles, (c) tree-level unitary is unachievable when the spin-2 particles transform under the adjoints of one or two spin-1 gauge groups

(i) it is possible to unitarize a theory that includes massive spin-1, spin-2 and scalar bosons, and (ii) it is not possible to unitarze a theory that only contains massive spin-2 or spin-1 and scalar bosons
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unitarization of tree-level 2 -> 2 scattering processes in a theory that only contains massive spin-2 particles.
the construction of a theory of massive spin-1, spin-2, and spin-0 particles that is both gauge invariant and unitary to very large momentum transfer.
the construction of unitary theories of massive spin-1, spin-2, and spin-0 particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it is possible to unitarize massive spin-2 interactions in the presence of massive spin-1 interactions, but not in the absence of them.

it is impossible for a theory with only massive spin-2, spin-1, and spin-0 particles, and only relevant and marginal interactions to be tree-level unitary at very high energy, unless the spin-1 particles are gauge bosons and the spin-2 particles are in the adjoint representation, and even then unitarity cannot be achieved in a theory with two spin-2 particles.

, for theories with only relevant and/or marginal operators, it is impossible to construct a unitary theory of massive spin-1 boson interactions, even if one includes spin-0 and spin-2 boson interactions, unless the spin-2 interactions are gauge invariant and the spin-1 interactions are gauge interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is impossible for a theory of massive spin-1, spin-2 and/or spin-0 boson fields to be unitarizable to very high energy, unless it is gauge invariant.

it is not possible to construct a unitary theory of massive spin-1, spin-2 and massless spin-2 boson interactions, where all interactions are gauge-invariant, without the addition of spin-0 boson fields.
it is possible to achieve tree-level 2-->2 unitarity for a theory of massive spin-0, spin-1, and spin-2 boson, but only if the spin-2 particles are not gauge bosons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the absence of a tree-level unitarized theory of massive spin- 2 bosons in the presence of gauge bosons is due to the fact that the spin-2 and gauge bosons are forced to couple to one another in the same way as they do in general relativity, which is not unitarizable at tree-level.
the unitarization of spin-2 scattering processes is very challenging in a theory with massive spin-2, spin-1 and scalar particles.

the unitarization of massive spin-1/2 and spin-1 boson scattering is not sufficient to unitarize massive spin-2 scattering, and the unitarization problem is more severe for spin-2 boson theories that are invariant under gauge symmetries.
